reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text:
Hi @clairlemon. I've been thinking about the possibility of 'conscious AI' since 2009 (https://t.co/VCtZaYIrXJ). I am a vocal skeptic, but I don't think it helps to characterise those who think AI might be conscious as 'insane'. Polarisation is dangerous, and the question of 'AI consciousness' is scientific, not political. There are good arguments on both side. IMO the sceptical arguments are far stronger, but others disagree & I respect and engage with their views. 

For a representative take on the state of the debate in academia, see this just-published @BBSJournal collection, which has my target article, 50 peer commentaries, and my response.  https://t.co/pzszCvMSgB
reviewedPosts.rationale: 有研究出版信息但偏概念

reviewedPosts.author: anilkseth
reviewedPosts.text: Indeed. I’ve a lot of respect for my colleagues in philosophy, neuroscience, and AI who are more open to the possibility of AI consciousness, and who make their case rationally. I still think they're wrong. But the issue is so important that it is a disservice to dismiss either side as deluded. https://t.co/vDvw82ookk

reviewedPosts.text: Yep, we are trying to figure out how best to add decode paths to Quail. Single or two-token projects (e.g., AI.CLASSIFY) are not so bad because they are still compute-bound. Scheduling gets tricky for open-ended AI MAP operators; we need to mix decode into prefill passes (we can try to "hide" decode under document reading). The challenge here is to be able to accurately estimate the length of an AI MAP operator output; so we can plan well

reviewedPosts.author: sh_reya
reviewedPosts.text: One of the most exciting parts of the Quail project (beyond the importance of the application) is how we are building it with agents. (1) We definitely do not want our agents to write all the code from scratch; we want to build on the battle-tested work of the community. (2) It is really important to credit the folks who build foundational infrastructure and algorithms; otherwise, there will be no incentive for people to continue doing foundational research. We see you and are really excited to build on top of what you do!
